spans.s: शस् in उक्थ-शस्, q. v.

शस् 1. शस् (said to be connected with
rt. 1. शम्, cf. rt. शष्), cl. 1. P. शसति,
शशास (3rd pl. शशसुः), शसितुम्, to cut, wound,
hurt, injure, strike, kill, destroy; [cf. Lat. hostia;
Goth. hunsl; Angl. Sax. husel.]

शस् 2. शस्, cl. 2. P. शस्ति, &c., to sleep,
= सस्, q. v.

शस् 3. शस्, the technical case-termination
of the accusative plural; the Taddhita affix शस् (form-
ing adverbs from nouns, especially from numerals
and words expressive of quantity, see शत-शस्,
बहु-शस्, &c.).

शश् शश्, cl. 1. P. शशति, शशाश, शशि-
तुम्, to jump, leap, spring, bound, dance;
A., Ved. to praise, laud, celebrate, (this sense ap-
pears to be doubtful and to result from a confusion
with शस् for rt. शंस्); [cf. Lith. szókti; Slav.
skakati, ‘to dance.’]

शष् शष् [cf. rt. 1. शस्], cl. 1. P. शषति,
शशाष, शषितुम्, to hurt, injure, strike,
wound, kill.

षष् षष्, षट्, m. f. n. pl. (thought by some
to be for an original स्वक्ष्, by others for क्षष्; षष्
becomes षट् before hard letters, षड् before soft, षो
before ड्, and षण् before nasals), six, (the following
words are used as symbolical expressions for the number
six, अङ्ग, दर्शन, तर्क, गुण, रस, ऋतु, वज्र-
कोण, कार्त्तिकेय-मुख); [cf. Zend kṣvas;
Gr. ἕξ, ϝέξ; Lat. sex; Angl. Sax. seox, sex, six;
Old Germ. sehs for sihs; Goth. saihs for sihs;
[]
Lith. szeszi, f. szezios; Slav. sesti, sesty; Cambro-
Brit. chwech; Armor. chuech; Hib. se, ‘six.’]
—षट्-कर्ण, अस्, आ, अम्, six-eared; heard by six
ears (i. e. by a third, instead of by the speaker and
person addressed only), told to more than one listener;
(अस्), m. a sort of lute.
—षट्-कर्मन्, अ, n. the
six acts or duties enjoined on Brāhmans collectively,
(viz. teaching the Vedas, holy study, offering sacri-
fices, conducting them for others, giving and accept-
ing gifts); six acts allowable to a Brāhman for sub-
sistence, (viz. gleaning, accepting gifts, asking alms,
agriculture, trade, tending cattle, or, according to
some, lending money at interest); six acts belonging
to the practice of Yoga, (viz., according to Śabda-k.,
धौति, वस्ति, नेति, नौलिकी, त्राटक, कपाल-
भाति, these consist of suppressions of the breath
and self-mortifications of various kinds; other
authorities write the words with different termi-
nations, e. g. धौती, वस्ती, नौलिक, &c.); six
acts that may be performed by means of magical
texts, (viz. killing, infatuating, enthralling, expelling,
exciting animosity, and the stopping or privation of
any faculty; these are taught in the Tantras); (आ),
m. a Brāhman skilled in the above six acts; an
adept in the Tantra magical rites.
